  "code": """"Measured LightGBM baseline for this tabular task."""

from __future__ import annotations

import pandas as pd
from lightgbm import LGBMClassifier


def fit_predict(train_csv: str, test_rows: list[dict[str, str]]) -> list[float]:
    train = pd.read_csv(train_csv)
    y = train.pop("y").astype(int)
    test = pd.DataFrame(test_rows, columns=list(train.columns))
    
    # Add missing value indicators for categorical fields with empty strings
    missing_cols = ['workclass', 'occupation']
    for col in missing_cols:
        if col in train.columns:
            train[col + '_missing'] = (train[col] == '').astype(int)
            test[col + '_missing'] = (test[col] == '').astype(int)
    
    for name in train.columns:
        if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(train[name]):
            test[name] = pd.to_numeric(test[name])
        else:
            # Replace empty strings with special MISSING marker
            train[name] = train[name].replace('', '<MISSING>')
            test[name] = test[name].replace('', '<MISSING>')
            categories = pd.Categorical(pd.concat([train[name], test[name]], ignore_index=True)).categories
            train[name] = pd.Categorical(train[name], categories=categories)
            test[name] = pd.Categorical(test[name], categories=categories)
    
    model = LGBMClassifier(random_state=20261114, n_jobs=1, verbosity=-1)
    model.fit(train, y)
    return model.predict_proba(test)[:, 1].tolist()
",
  "notes": "Added two missing value indicator columns (workclass_missing, occupation_missing) that flag rows with empty string values. Also replaced empty strings with '<MISSING>' before categorical encoding so the model learns that missing is distinct from valid category values. This addresses the observed pattern where some samples (e.g., age=17) have blank workclass/occupation."
